raw_segments.text: When I got home at night, and delivered this message for Joe, my sister, went on the rampage,
in a more alarming degree than at any previous period.
She asked me and Joe whether we supposed she was doormats under our feet, and how we dared
to use her so, and what company we graciously thought she was fit for.
When she had exhausted a torrent of such inquiries, she threw a candlestick at Joe, burst into
a loud sobbing, got out the dustpan, which was always a very bad sign, put on her coarse
apron, and began cleaning up to a terrible extent.
Not satisfied with a dry cleaning, she took to a pail and scrubbing brush, and cleaned
us out of house and home, so that we stood shivering in the backyard.
It was ten o'clock at night before we ventured to creep in again, and then she asked Joe
why he hadn't married a negress slave at once.
Joe offered no answer, poor fellow, but stood feeling his whisker and looking dejectedly
at me, as if he thought it really might have been a better speculation.
